deep.reconstruction:
The page holds four unrelated computations, written in October 1855 with a later addition dated October 1856.

(A) Implicit differentiation on a plane curve f(x,y)=0. Along the curve dy = -(f_x/f_y) dx. Hence d(f_y) = f_yx dx + f_yy dy = (f_y f_yx - f_yy f_x)/f_y dx. Riemann writes this as d log f_y = (f_y f_yx - f_yy f_x)/f_y^2 dx. The first line, f_yx = f_yy f_x/f_y, is the condition that this logarithmic differential vanishes, i.e. that f_y stays constant along the curve. Probably this is a preliminary to studying the integrand dx/f_y.

(B) Theta function and its periodicity.
- Definition: Theta(u) = sum over m in Z^p of exp( sum_{mu,mu'} a_{mu mu'} m_mu m_mu' + 2 sum_mu m_mu u_mu ).
- Period table: u_mu -> u_mu + pi*i (the mu-th column of pi*i*I) leaves Theta unchanged.
- Shift by a column of the symmetric matrix (a): u -> u + a_{.,nu} multiplies Theta by a factor. log Theta changes by -2u_nu - a_{nu nu}; the page writes the case nu=1, -2u_1 - a_{11}.
- Derivation (mine): Q(m+e_1) = Q(m) + 2(am)_1 + a_11. Re-indexing m -> m+e_1 gives Theta(u + a e_1) = exp(-2u_1 - a_11) Theta(u).

(C) Change of canonical cross-cut system (transformation of the period moduli).
- The new cuts a', b' are related to the old a, b by an integer 2p x 2p matrix. Its entries are written (mu a / mu' a), (mu a / mu' b), etc., e.g. kappa^{mu a}_alpha = sum_mu' (mu a/mu' a) kappa'^{mu' a}_alpha + (mu a/mu' b) kappa'^{mu' b}_alpha.
- The inverse matrix, in square brackets, is stated to be [mu' b/mu b] = (mu a/mu' a), [mu' b/mu a] = -(mu b/mu' a), [mu' a/mu b] = -(mu a/mu' b), [mu' a/mu a] = (mu b/mu' b).
- In modern terms: for M = [[A,B],[C,D]] symplectic, M^{-1} = [[D^T, -B^T], [-C^T, A^T]].
- He then substitutes into the alternating form sum_mu (kappa^{mu a}_alpha kappa^{mu b}_beta - kappa^{mu b}_alpha kappa^{mu a}_beta) = 0. This is Riemann's bilinear period relation for two integrals of the first kind. Its preservation under the change of cuts is the symplectic condition on the integer matrix.
- The tables headed phi' and phi write out M and its inverse explicitly (inverse = transpose with sign changes).

(D) Transformation and parity of theta characteristics.
- He writes alpha'_1 = alpha_1(1a/1a) + ... + alpha_p(pa/1a) + beta_1(1b/1a) + ... + beta_p(pb/1a), and similarly beta'_1.
- He writes (beta'_1..beta'_p, -alpha'_1..-alpha'_p) = phi'(beta_1..beta_p, -alpha_1..-alpha_p).
- He begins to compute beta'_1 alpha'_1 + ... + beta'_p alpha'_p, i.e. how the parity sum alpha.beta mod 2 of a half-period characteristic behaves under the transformation.
- Counting characteristics: each coordinate pair (alpha_i, beta_i) in (Z/2)^2 has product 1 in one of 4 cases. So the number of odd characteristics is sum_{k odd} C(p,k) 3^{p-k} = p 3^{p-1} + C(p,3) 3^{p-3} + ... = ((3+1)^p - (3-1)^p)/2 = (4^p - 2^p)/2 = 2^{p-1}(2^p - 1).
- He records the total number 2^{2p}, the identity 2^p(2^p-1)/2 = 2^{p-1}(2^p-1), and also ((2^{p+1}-1)^2 - 1)/8 = 2^{p-1}(2^p-1). All are equal; for p=3 the count is 28 (bitangents of the plane quartic).

(E) Plane model of degree n = 2p-2 (the image of the curve under ratios of first-kind integrands, written x(mu,eta,xi) of degree 2p-2).
- Genus formula: p = (n-1)(n-2)/2 - r with r double points. With n = 2p-2: r = (2p-3)(p-2) - p = 2p^2 - 8p + 6 = 2(p-1)(p-3) = 2((p-2)^2 - 1). This requires p >= 3; p=3 gives a smooth quartic.
- Intersections with f_x = 0 (degree 2p-3): there are (2p-2)(2p-3). Each node absorbs 2, leaving (2p-2)(2p-3) - 2r = 6p - 6 = 2p + 2(2p-3) branch points. This agrees with Riemann-Hurwitz, w = 2n + 2p - 2.
- Adjoint curves of degree n-3 = 2p-5: there are (2p-3)(2p-4)/2 coefficients, minus r conditions, giving (2p-3)(p-2) - 2(p-2)^2 + 2 = p. That is the number of first-kind differentials phi dy/f_x.
- For degree n-4 = 2p-6 he notes (2p-4)(2p-5)/2 = (p-2)(2p-5) = 2p^2 - 9p + 10 = r - p + 4.
- He also records (2p-4)(2p-3)/2 + 3(p-2) = 2p(p-2), and r + p - 3 = 2p^2 - 7p + 3.
errors: No genuine mathematical errors found. All the numerical identities check.

The line '(2p-4)(2p-?)/1.2 + 3(p-2) = 2p(p-2)' holds only if the faint factor is (2p-3). With (2p-5), as the machine transcription has it, the left side is 2(p-1)(p-2). The image is more consistent with (2p-3); this is a transcription issue, not Riemann's error.
The first line f_yx = f_yy f_x/f_y is stated without context. It is a condition (vanishing of d log f_y along the curve), not an identity.

results.what: Quasi-periodicity of the p-variable theta series: invariance under pi*i shifts; factor exp(-2u_nu - a_{nu nu}) under shift by a column of the symmetric matrix (a)
results.modern_name: Quasi-periodicity of the Riemann theta function

results.what: Inverse of the integer transformation matrix of the cross-cuts given by transpose with sign changes, and preservation of the bilinear period relation
results.modern_name: Symplectic group Sp(2p,Z) acting on period matrices; Riemann bilinear relations
results.usually_credited_to: Hermite 1855 (p=2 transformation); Riemann 1857 (bilinear relations); general transformation theory: Weber, Thomae, Frobenius, Kronecker

results.what: Number of odd theta characteristics in genus p: 2^{p-1}(2^p-1), via sum over odd k of C(p,k)3^{p-k}; total 2^{2p}
results.modern_name: Count of odd/even theta characteristics (odd: 2^{p-1}(2^p-1), even: 2^{p-1}(2^p+1))
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (lectures; Weber 1876 for p=3), Clebsch-Gordan 1866; Goepel/Rosenhain for p=2

results.what: Behaviour of the characteristic parity sum alpha.beta under a symplectic change of cuts (transformation of characteristics)
results.modern_name: Transformation law of theta characteristics under Sp(2p,Z); invariance of parity

results.what: Plane model of degree 2p-2 has r = 2(p-1)(p-3) double points; 6p-6 branch points; adjoint curves of degree n-3 give exactly p first-kind differentials
results.modern_name: Plane projection of the canonical curve; genus/Pluecker formula; Riemann-Hurwitz; adjoint curves (Brill-Noether)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 (s,z from ratios of phi's, degree 2p-2); Clebsch, Brill-Noether 1874

deep.surprise_reason: Everything here matches material Riemann published in 1857 or is attributed to him through Weber's editions: theta periodicity, the bilinear relations, the plane model of degree 2p-2, and the adjoint count. The explicit general-p count of odd characteristics, together with a start on their transformation, dated October 1855/56, is a mildly notable dating detail but not a new attribution.

transcription_corrections: Line read as '(2p-4)(2p-5)/1.2 + 3(p-2) = 2p(p-2)' should most likely be '(2p-4)(2p-3)/1.2 + 3(p-2) = 2p(p-2)'. Only that version is a valid identity.
'Gem. W.' is plausibly 'gemeinschaftliche Werthe' (common points/intersections) of f with f_x, resp. with f_y and f_x; 'Anz. d. dy' is 'Anzahl der' (number of) branch points in dy.
'x(mu,eta,xi)^{2p-2}' likely denotes a homogeneous form of degree 2p-2 in coordinates (mu? or x, eta, xi), i.e. the plane curve of degree 2p-2.
The marginal date 'October 1856' is a separate later annotation next to the d log f_y formula; the page header is 'October 1855'.
